For stride-one causal convolutions, the maximum receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σℓ(kℓ−1)dℓ, counting every temporal convolution along the longest residual path. Two convolutions per block must both contribute; 1×1 convolutions add no temporal span. Residual additions take unions of dependencies. Exact reachable positions may have dilation-induced holes. NextItNet has multiple residual-block designs, so calculate from the implemented layers, rather than block names. [Receptive-field derivation](https://distill.pub/2019/computing-receptive-fields/), [NextItNet paper](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/182377/2/182377.pdf).

Normalization can invalidate this convolution-only bound. On tensors shaped [B,L,C], LayerNorm(C) normalizes channels independently at each position; LayerNorm([L,C]) mixes time. GroupNorm on [B,C,L] also aggregates temporal positions. BatchNorm1d mixes batch and time during training; evaluation with frozen running statistics is local, whereas disabling running statistics retains coupling. Thus, architectural inference: outside-field invariance requires every path to the readout to preserve temporal locality—local embeddings, correctly padded causal convolutions, pointwise operations and channel-only normalization—with no global pooling, temporal normalization, attention, or input-dependent global gates. Read the final nonpadding position; for left padding, never use count−1. [LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html), [GroupNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.GroupNorm.html), [BatchNorm1d](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.BatchNorm1d.html).

Verify the actual predictor with fixed weights in deterministic evaluation mode: preserve sequence length, padding, positions, candidate IDs and the final R inputs; repeatedly replace only earlier nonpadding tokens. Compare final features and raw scores within numerical tolerance. Probe gradients with respect to input embeddings as an additional check. A changed score disproves locality; unchanged scores or zero gradients alone cannot prove it because saturation or inactive paths can hide dependencies. The guarantee comes from auditing the complete computation graph, including normalization axes.
